title: The Brave Little Tailor
text:
A little tailor swatted the flies on his jam bread and killed seven at one blow. Delighted, he stitched a belt reading "Seven at One Blow" and set out to see the world.

On a mountain he met a giant who read the belt and assumed it meant seven men. The giant squeezed a stone until water ran out; the tailor squeezed a soft cheese he had in his pocket until whey dripped. The giant threw a stone so high it was hard to see; the tailor threw a bird, which flew away and never came down. The giant carried a tree trunk; the tailor offered to carry the branches and simply rode on them. Invited to sleep in the giants' cave, he found the bed too big and lay in a corner, so when a giant smashed the bed with an iron bar in the night, the tailor survived, and the giants fled in terror when they saw him in the morning.

His fame reached the king, who promised him half the kingdom and his daughter if he killed two giants terrorizing the forest. The tailor climbed a tree above the sleeping giants and dropped stones on one, then the other. Each thought the other had hit him, and they fought until both were dead.

After more tasks, the tailor married the princess and became king.
lesson: Strength is only one kind of power. Reputation, nerve and a clear reading of an opponent's temper can let a small player win against much bigger ones.
people: The tailor, the giants, the king
source: Brothers Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmarchen, No. 20
